prompt: A tree casts a shadow $20$ ft long. From the tip of the shadow, the angle of elevation up to the top of the tree is $45^\circ$. How tall is the tree, in feet?
hint: Draw the right triangle: the shadow is the bottom, the tree is the upright side.

hints.text: Draw the right triangle: the shadow is the bottom, the tree is the upright side.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: a $10$ ft shadow with a $45^\circ$ elevation gives a $10$ ft pole, because $\tan(45^\circ) = 1$ makes height equal shadow. Same move, bigger number.
From the shadow tip, the tree is opposite and the shadow is adjacent: $\tan(45^\circ) = \frac{h}{20}$.

explanation: Angle of elevation is measured UP from the flat ground.
The tree is opposite that angle and the shadow is adjacent, so use TOA: $\tan(45^\circ) = \frac{h}{20}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: It is a 45-45-90 triangle
steps: One angle is $90^\circ$ and another is $45^\circ$, so the last one is $45^\circ$ too.
Two equal angles mean two equal legs.
The shadow leg is $20$ ft, so the tree leg is also $20$ ft.

alternativeExplanations.title: The shadow rule of thumb
steps: When the sun sits at $45^\circ$, every object casts a shadow exactly as long as it is tall.
So the tree stands $20$ ft tall.
